q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a shock absorber?
title: Shock absorber carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the steel tubes, rod, spring, oil and seals per shock absorber and multiply by supplier figures. Add machining, plating, welding, assembly and painting energy, then divide the plant's energy by units made.
audience: Shock absorber and suspension part makers

ul: Steel tubes and chrome-plated piston rod.
Assembly, oil filling, testing and painting.

p: Report per unit by vehicle type and weight.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 71,000 / 100,000 = 0.710 kg CO2 per unit
Add steel, spring and oil for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
